item.title: Les Leyne: B.C. sidelines housing projects while pushing cities to keep up pace
item.description: If the province can delay its own housing plans, why is it still holding municipalities to targets designed for a market that no longer exists?

item.title: B.C. January home sales off to a slow start in 2026
item.description: Greater Vancouver led monthly real estate sales declines, while B.C.’s inflation rate increased in January 2026

item.title: B.C. forestry sector beaten to a pulp
item.description: Vancouver's Canfor to bring pulp division back into fold due to less global demand

item.title: Rob Shaw: Eby caught in contradiction over Musqueam title agreement
item.description: Premier claims he wasn't briefed on deal signed a few feet away from him last month

item.title: Vancouver home transactions down in February as sellers holding off: board
item.description: Vancouver-area home sales continued at slower pace last month compared to last year as prices were also lower. There were 1,648 sales of residential properties in the region throughout February, down 9.8 per cent from the same month in 2025 and 28.

item.title: Rising foreign investment in Canada doesn't tell the whole story, economists say
item.description: OTTAWA — Statistics Canada says the flow of foreign direct investment into the economy came close to a two-decade high last year, while economists caution the volume of capital entering Canada isn't the only metric that matters.

item.title: S&P/TSX composite tumbles 2 per cent, U.S. markets also down on Mideast war fears
item.description: TORONTO — Canada's main stock index dived, then pared back some of its losses to finish the day 2.2 per cent lower on Tuesday as investors worried about a widening of the war between Iran and the United States and Israel.

item.title: B.C.'s move to end clock changes won't be without complications
item.description: The mayor of Prince George in northern British Columbia is the father of six adult children, who got used to the struggle of getting his kids out of bed on dark winter mornings as they were growing up.

item.title: Vancouver crypto platform director admits fraud, pays $1M
item.description: Michael Ongun Gokturk is permanently banned from B.C. investment market

item.title: Carney in Australia to deepen trade and defence ties with 'natural partner'
item.description: SYDNEY — Prime Minister Mark Carney is in Australia, where he says his government is focused on forging new partnerships in investment, defence, security, critical minerals and artificial intelligence.
